affiliations.date_precision: In testimony recorded during the Board's May-June 1944 proceedings, Chrysostomas said he entered OSS 'last July' and had been with the 19th Communications Squadron when he was transferred; July 1943 is therefore date-bounded to month precision.
affiliations.research_notes: This is an explicitly documented Army-to-OSS transfer, not a civilian employer. The source says the OSS needed a Greek-speaking radio teacher.

affiliations.date_precision: The rare exact-name Army entry dated 16 January 1941 carries occupation value 024; actual work dates and whether the value describes paid employment, teaching or musical work are unestablished.
affiliations.research_notes: The code is corroborated to this rare-name identity by the exact Army-entry date in Chrysostomas's direct testimony, but it names no employer or institution and is not reconciled into a single occupation with his documented student status.

affiliations.date_precision: The official Army entry dated 26 August 1943 carries occupation value 992, which the NARA code list labels Students; the institution, attendance dates and temporal relationship to OSS service are unestablished.

claims.claim_text: The indexed George Chrysostomas is confirmed as Captain George Christy Chrysostomas of OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A direct 1944 OSS Board interview names George Christy Chrysostomas, gives the same printed number sequence with an officer prefix, and records the same 16 January 1941 Army-entry date as the rare exact-name Army row.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the rare exact first and last name, the direct OSS context, the matching printed number sequence, the matching Army-entry date and a contemporary OCS notice.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Board interviewed him in the Middle East theater in 1944 and recorded his Army entry, 1942 officer-candidate training, July 1943 OSS transfer and current radio-school work.
claims.match_notes: George Christy Chrysostomas is retained as a documented name variant. The index's six-digit value is preserved unchanged; no leading character is silently added and no full identifier is published.

claims.claim_text: George Chrysostomas's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the U.S. Army's 19th Communications Squadron in the Middle East theater.
claims.evidence_excerpt: I was in this theater with the 19th Communications Squadron
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Chrysostomas said that he was serving with the 19th Communications Squadron when OSS transferred him because it needed someone who could teach radio in Greek.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by direct-person wartime testimony and the independently corroborated rare-name identity.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly immediate: the witness described the squadron as the assignment from which he was transferred into OSS, which he dated to the preceding July.
claims.match_notes: Modeled as a military assignment, not a civilian employer. The unit name is preserved as found; no unsupported parent command or modern successor is added.
